note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old woman with 3–4 days of constant, worsening midline lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain (8/10) with light pink vaginal spotting and mild discharge; pregnancy to be excluded urgently. Face-to-face exam and same-day home pregnancy test arranged.

History:
- Presenting complaint/timeline: Constant lower abdominal pain, below the umbilicus, midline, started a few days ago; progressively worsening; severity ~8/10. Nausea without vomiting. Able to eat/drink and continue activities but uncomfortable.
- Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding/spotting outside menses; slight vaginal discharge. No dyspnea, no shoulder-tip pain, no fever/rigors, no presyncope on standing.
- GI: Constipation for about a week last week (now resolved). No diarrhea reported. No reported blood in stool.
- GU: No dysuria, no malodorous urine. Denies difficulty passing urine. Urinary frequency unclear from history.
- Gynecologic/obstetric: Sexually active; last intercourse ~4 days ago. Contraceptive implant (Implanon/Nexplanon) placed ~1 year ago; menses occur but irregular. Last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago; last period was reported as normal. Last pregnancy test ~1 month ago (none since pain began). G0 (no prior pregnancies).
- Past medical/surgical: No surgeries reported; no chronic conditions reported.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Medications: Contraceptive implant; no other regular medications mentioned.
- Social: School teacher. Lives with husband and husband’s family. Denies recreational drug use. Smoking/alcohol use unclear. No recent travel (last abroad ~1 year ago).

Examination:
- No vitals obtained (teleconsultation).
- No physical exam performed; in-person abdominal/pelvic exam planned.

Impression:
- Working clinical impression: Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting. Must exclude pregnancy-related causes.
- Top differential diagnoses (from DDx and consistent with transcript):
  1) Ectopic pregnancy (medium likelihood; urgent rule-out): Pelvic pain with light bleeding; sexually active; no pregnancy test since symptom onset; implant reduces but does not eliminate risk.
  2) Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) (medium likelihood): Lower abdominal pain with spotting and mild discharge; sexually active; may occur without fever.
  3) Functional/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst (medium likelihood): Acute pelvic pain and irregular bleeding; can occur with implant use.
- Other considerations: Appendicitis (low–medium; pain is midline without classic RLQ localization or fever). Cystitis/UTI less likely given lack of urinary symptoms.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  - Home urine pregnancy test today; if positive, patient to call back immediately for urgent assessment.
  - Arrange face-to-face clinic evaluation via support line for abdominal and pelvic examination.
  - Safety-net: Seek urgent care if pain significantly worsens, heavy vaginal bleeding, inability to keep fluids down, syncope/presyncope, new shoulder-tip pain, or fever.
- At in-person visit (next steps consistent with DDx and presentation):
  - Repeat urine pregnancy test in clinic if not already done; quantitative serum hCG if positive or high suspicion.
  - Pelvic exam to assess cervical motion/adnexal tenderness; STI testing (NAAT for chlamydia/gonorrhea).
  - Urinalysis/urine culture if urinary symptoms develop or suspicion persists.
  - Pelvic ultrasound if pregnancy test positive or if pelvic pathology suspected (ectopic, ovarian cyst).
  - Basic labs as indicated (CBC, CRP) if concern for infection or appendicitis.
- Symptomatic care:
  - Maintain hydration. Consider simple analgesia (e.g., acetaminophen) pending in-person assessment (not explicitly discussed in transcript).

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals; abdominal/pelvic exam; formal review of urinary frequency; STI risk assessment; smoking and alcohol history; complete medication list; documented follow-up timing/date.
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted. DDx reasoning aligns with transcript. Where urinary frequency is discussed, transcript is unclear; DDx treats UTI as less likely.
● Transcript quality:
  - Audio/text intermittently unclear with incomplete responses and overlaps; several items remain ambiguous (e.g., urinary frequency, weight loss, blood in stool/urine, smoking/alcohol).
